Calcar.question: The _____ was Spur of cartilage in bats.

Chondrichthyes.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Chondrichthyes.question: The _____ was Class of jawed cartilaginous fish.
Chondrichthyes.fact: Chondrichthyes (; from Ancient Greek χόνδρος (khóndros) 'cartilage' and ἰχθύς (ikhthús) 'fish') is a class of jawed fish that contains the cartilaginous fish or chondrichthyans, which all have skeletons primarily composed of cartilage. Chondrichthyes are aquatic vertebrates with paired fins, paired nares, placoid scales, and conus arteriosus in the heart.

Chondrichthyes.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Chondrichthyes.question: They can be contrasted with the _____ or bony fish, which have skeletons primarily composed of bone tissue
Chondrichthyes.fact: They can be contrasted with the Osteichthyes or bony fish, which have skeletons primarily composed of bone tissue.

Chondrichthyes.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Chondrichthyes.question: Within the infraphylum _____, cartilaginous fishes are distinct from all other jawed vertebrates
Chondrichthyes.fact: Within the infraphylum Gnathostomata, cartilaginous fishes are distinct from all other jawed vertebrates.

Chondrichthyes.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Chondrichthyes.question: The notochord is gradually replaced by a vertebral column during development, except in _____, where the notochord stays intact
Chondrichthyes.fact: The class is divided into two subclasses: Elasmobranchii (sharks, rays, skates and sawfish) which lack opercula, and Holocephali (chimaeras, sometimes called ghost sharks, which are sometimes separated into their own class). The notochord is gradually replaced by a vertebral column during development, except in Holocephali, where the notochord stays intact.

Chondrichthyes.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Chondrichthyes.question: They are also produced in the _____'s organ, which is only found in certain cartilaginous fishes
Chondrichthyes.fact: They are also produced in the Leydig's organ, which is only found in certain cartilaginous fishes. The subclass Holocephali, which is a very specialized group, lacks both the Leydig's and epigonal organs.

Chondrichthyes.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Chondrichthyes.question: The subclass _____, which is a very specialized group, lacks both the Leydig's and epigonal organs
Chondrichthyes.fact: The subclass Holocephali, which is a very specialized group, lacks both the Leydig's and epigonal organs.

Circle of death (boating).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circle of death (boating).question: The _____ was Motorboating hazard.
Circle of death (boating).fact: The circle of death is a hazardous phenomenon experienced by motorboats. A circle of death can be initiated if the boat operator releases the steering mechanism while the boat is still powered, which means the propeller is still turning.

Circuit training.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circuit training.question: The _____ was Conditioning training method with consecutive exercises.
Circuit training.fact: Circuit training is a form of body conditioning that involves endurance training, resistance training, high-intensity aerobics, and exercises performed in a circuit, similar to high-intensity interval training.

Circumference.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circumference.question: The _____ was Perimeter of a circle or ellipse.
Circumference.fact: In geometry, the circumference (from Latin circumferēns 'carrying around, circling') is the perimeter of a circle or ellipse. The circumference is the arc length of the circle, as if it were opened up and straightened out to a line segment.

Circumference.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Circumference.fact: This constant, pi, is represented by the Greek letter π.

Circumference.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Circumference.fact: The last such calculation was performed in 1630 by Christoph Grienberger who used polygons with 1040 sides.

Circumference.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circumference.question: One common intrinsic definition is by _____ measure
Circumference.fact: One common intrinsic definition is by Hausdorff measure. If E {\displaystyle E} is a subset of the Euclidean plane, its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is obtained by covering E {\displaystyle E} with sets of small diameter and taking the infimum of the sums of those diameters.

Circumscription (taxonomy).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circumscription (taxonomy).question: The _____ was Definition of a taxon.
Circumscription (taxonomy).fact: In biological taxonomy, circumscription is the content of a taxon, that is, the delimitation of which subordinate taxa are parts of that taxon. For example, if it is determined that species X, Y, and Z belong in genus A, and species T, U, V, and W belong in genus B, those are the circumscriptions of those two genera.

Circumscription (taxonomy).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circumscription (taxonomy).question: For example, the family _____ contained orangutans (Pongo), chimpanzees (Pan) and gorillas (Gorilla), but not humans (Homo), which are placed in Hominidae
Circumscription (taxonomy).fact: For example, the family Pongidae contained orangutans (Pongo), chimpanzees (Pan) and gorillas (Gorilla), but not humans (Homo), which are placed in Hominidae. Once molecular phylogenetic data showed that chimpanzees were more closely related to humans than to gorillas or orangutans, it became clear that Pongidae is a paraphyletic group, and the circumscription of Hominidae was changed to include all four extant genera of great apes.

Circumscription (taxonomy).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circumscription (taxonomy).question: For example, the broadly circumscribed monophyletic moth superfamily _____ can be split into two families, Pyralidae and Crambidae, which are reciprocally monophyletic sister taxa
Circumscription (taxonomy).fact: For example, the broadly circumscribed monophyletic moth superfamily Pyraloidea can be split into two families, Pyralidae and Crambidae, which are reciprocally monophyletic sister taxa.

Circumscription (taxonomy).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Circumscription (taxonomy).question: An example of a botanical group with unstable circumscription is _____, a family of flowering plants
Circumscription (taxonomy).fact: An example of a botanical group with unstable circumscription is Anacardiaceae, a family of flowering plants.

Circumscription (taxonomy).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Cisuralian.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cisuralian.question: The name "Cisuralian" was proposed in _____, and approved by the International Subcommission on Permian Stratigraphy in 1996

Cisuralian.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cisuralian.question: In northwestern Europe, the _____ orogeny continued
Cisuralian.fact: In northwestern Europe, the Hercynian orogeny continued.

Cisuralian.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cisuralian.question: This created the large supercontinent, Pangea, by the middle of the early _____, which was to have an impact on the climate

This created the large supercontinent, Pangea, by the middle of the early Permian, which was to have an impact on the climate.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: The _____ was Method of biological systematics in evolutionary biology.
Cladistics.fact: Cladistics ( klə-DIST-iks; from Ancient Greek κλάδος kládos 'branch') is an approach to biological classification in which organisms are categorized in groups ("clades") based on hypotheses of most recent common ancestry.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: What is now called the cladistic method appeared as early as _____ with a work by Peter Chalmers Mitchell for birds and subsequently by Robert John Tillyard (for insects) in 1921, and W. Zimmermann (f
Cladistics.fact: What is now called the cladistic method appeared as early as 1901 with a work by Peter Chalmers Mitchell for birds and subsequently by Robert John Tillyard (for insects) in 1921, and W. Zimmermann (for plants) in 1943.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: What is now called the cladistic method appeared as early as 1901 with a work by _____ for birds and subsequently by Robert John Tillyard (for insects) in 1921, and W. Zimmermann (for plants) in 1943
Cladistics.fact: What is now called the cladistic method appeared as early as 1901 with a work by Peter Chalmers Mitchell for birds and subsequently by Robert John Tillyard (for insects) in 1921, and W. Zimmermann (for plants) in 1943.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: Phenetics was championed at this time by the numerical taxonomists _____ and Robert Sokal, and evolutionary taxonomy by Ernst Mayr
Cladistics.fact: Phenetics was championed at this time by the numerical taxonomists Peter Sneath and Robert Sokal, and evolutionary taxonomy by Ernst Mayr.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: Originally conceived, if only in essence, by Willi Hennig in a book published in _____, cladistics did not flourish until its translation into English in 1966 (Lewin 1997)
Cladistics.fact: Originally conceived, if only in essence, by Willi Hennig in a book published in 1950, cladistics did not flourish until its translation into English in 1966 (Lewin 1997).

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: Within the primates, all anthropoids (monkeys, apes, and humans) are hypothesized to have had a common ancestor all of whose descendants are or were anthropoids, so they form the clade called _____
Cladistics.fact: Within the primates, all anthropoids (monkeys, apes, and humans) are hypothesized to have had a common ancestor all of whose descendants are or were anthropoids, so they form the clade called Anthropoidea. The name Prosimii is not used in phylogenetic nomenclature, which names only clades; the "prosimians" are instead divided between the clades Strepsirhini and Haplorhini, where the latter contains Tarsiiformes and Anthropoidea.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: For example, _____ is traditionally characterized by (among other things) being cold-blooded (i.e., not maintaining a constant high body temperature), whereas birds are warm-blooded
Cladistics.fact: For example, Reptilia is traditionally characterized by (among other things) being cold-blooded (i.e., not maintaining a constant high body temperature), whereas birds are warm-blooded.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: For example, the possession of digits that are homologous with those of _____ sapiens is a synapomorphy within the vertebrates
Cladistics.fact: For example, the possession of digits that are homologous with those of Homo sapiens is a synapomorphy within the vertebrates. The tetrapods can be singled out as consisting of the first vertebrate with such digits homologous to those of Homo sapiens together with all descendants of this vertebrate (an apomorphy-based phylogenetic definition).

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: Anthropology and archaeology: _____ methods have been used to reconstruct the development of cultures or artifacts using groups of cultural traits or artifact features
Cladistics.fact: Anthropology and archaeology: Cladistic methods have been used to reconstruct the development of cultures or artifacts using groups of cultural traits or artifact features. Comparative mythology and folktale use cladistic methods to reconstruct the protoversion of many myths.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: The term "clade" was introduced in _____ by Julian Huxley after having been coined by Lucien Cuénot in 1940,
Cladistics.fact: The term "clade" was introduced in 1958 by Julian Huxley after having been coined by Lucien Cuénot in 1940, "cladogenesis" in 1958, "cladistic" by Arthur Cain and Harrison in 1960, "cladist" (for an adherent of Hennig's school) by Ernst Mayr in 1965, and "cladistics" in 1966.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: Mythological phylogenies constructed with mythemes clearly support low horizontal transmissions (borrowings), historical (sometimes _____) diffusions and punctuated evolution
Cladistics.fact: Mythological phylogenies constructed with mythemes clearly support low horizontal transmissions (borrowings), historical (sometimes Palaeolithic) diffusions and punctuated evolution.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: Literature: _____ methods have been used in the classification of the surviving manuscripts of the Canterbury Tales, and the manuscripts of the Sanskrit Charaka Samhita
Cladistics.fact: Comparative mythology and folktale use cladistic methods to reconstruct the protoversion of many myths. Literature: Cladistic methods have been used in the classification of the surviving manuscripts of the Canterbury Tales, and the manuscripts of the Sanskrit Charaka Samhita.

Cladistics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladistics.question: Historical linguistics: _____ methods have been used to reconstruct the phylogeny of languages using linguistic features
Cladistics.fact: Literature: Cladistic methods have been used in the classification of the surviving manuscripts of the Canterbury Tales, and the manuscripts of the Sanskrit Charaka Samhita. Historical linguistics: Cladistic methods have been used to reconstruct the phylogeny of languages using linguistic features.

Cladogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladogenesis.question: The _____ was Evolutionary splitting of a parent species into two distinct species, forming a clade.
Cladogenesis.fact: Cladogenesis is an evolutionary splitting of a parent species into two distinct species, forming a new clade that contains two newly separated lineages—with one common ancestor. Cladogenesis typically occurs after a few organisms of an original population are abruptly transported to new or distant areas, or after environmental changes cause extinction(s) that open up new ecological niches for the survivors—or that cause population bottlenecks and founder effects that change allele frequencies...

Cladogram.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladogram.question: The _____ was Diagram used to show relations among groups of organisms with common origins.
Cladogram.fact: A cladogram (from Greek κλάδος klados "branch" and γραμμα gramma "character") is a diagram used in cladistics to show evolutionary relations (common descent) between groups of organisms. Cladograms are a type (subset) of phylogenetic trees that do not normally show evolutionary time but are required to meet specific criteria defined by cladistics.

Cladogram.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cladogram.question: Approaches such as maximum likelihood, which incorporate explicit models of sequence evolution, are non-_____ ways to evaluate sequence data
Cladogram.fact: Approaches such as maximum likelihood, which incorporate explicit models of sequence evolution, are non-Hennigian ways to evaluate sequence data.

Clamp (tool).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Clamp (tool).question: The _____ was Fastening tool.
Clamp (tool).fact: A clamp is a fastening device used to hold or secure objects tightly together to prevent movement or separation through the application of inward pressure. In the United Kingdom the term cramp is often used instead when the tool is for temporary use for positioning components during construction and woodworking; thus a G cramp or a sash clamp but a wheel clamp or a surgical clamp.

Clapstick.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Clapstick.question: The _____ was Traditional Australian Aboriginal instrument.
Clapstick.fact: Clapsticks, also spelt clap sticks and also called bilma, bimli, clappers, musicstick or just stick, are a traditional Australian Aboriginal instrument. Unlike drumsticks, which are generally used to strike a drum, clapsticks are intended for striking one stick on another.

Clapstick.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Clapstick.question: They serve to maintain rhythm in voice chants, often as part of an _____ ceremony
Clapstick.fact: Clapsticks, also spelt clap sticks and also called bilma, bimli, clappers, musicstick or just stick, are a traditional Australian Aboriginal instrument. They serve to maintain rhythm in voice chants, often as part of an Aboriginal ceremony.

Clarifying agent.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Clarifying agent.question: The _____ was Agent used to remove suspended solids from liquid.
Clarifying agent.fact: Clarifying agents are used to remove suspended solids from liquids by inducing flocculation, causing the solids to form larger aggregates that can be easily removed after they either float to the surface or sink to the bottom of the containment vessel.
